idiom_name: class with private members and constructor-established invariants
implementation_notes: C++ provides the classic structure directly: a class with private data members, a constructor that establishes the invariant and public methods that preserve it (C++ Core Guidelines C.2/C.3), enum class for closed value sets, and value-semantic classes for value objects (copy, equality, hashing). No framework is required - domain types are plain persistence-ignorant classes, while mapping lives in separate mapper/repository translation units. The classic form is justified whenever several members must stay consistent (a type with an invariant); for data whose members vary independently, a plain struct is the better model.
pitfalls: Public data members (or a friend mapper) let callers bypass the invariant; keep state private and expose only intent-named methods.
Value semantics copy the object: polymorphic members are sliced on copy - decide deliberately between closed value types, references or smart pointers instead of relying on the generated copy.
Domain headers must not include persistence headers; if a domain class seems to need the database, that responsibility belongs to a mapper or repository.
